segments.summary: Reviewed F-028 through F-034 exactly and adversarially: the units establish large-file, shortcut, persistence, accessibility, mention, shared-context, and open-routing intent, while leaving material boundary, lifecycle, race, authority, and path-hardening behavior to builders.

Reviewed F-035 through F-041: approval-scoped artifact visibility, route and ref families, artifact resolution, recovery, and tab identities have unresolved typed, authority, revocation, and transition contracts; F-041's restored section ownership is an explicit non-gap.

Reviewed F-042 through F-048: navigation fallbacks, sparse editor seams, symbol status, diagnostics, semantic actions, and chat references lack freshness, provider merge, projection revision, mutation-apply, and access-lifecycle semantics.

Reviewed F-049 through F-055: command and ownership boundaries are clearer than the operational contracts; destructive menus, clipboard moves, transfers, filters, Open With, and copy-out need exact guards, state machines, integrity, and partial-failure recovery.

Reviewed F-056 through F-062: Source Control and diff/review handoffs remain under-specified across commands, owner routing, stale targets, hunk authority, reconciliation, and exact revert identity despite strong negative constraints.

Reviewed F-063 through F-067 plus retired F-001 and Migration Coverage: restore events and cross-surface diff state lack transition protocols; F-001 is safely lineage-only; F-067 and the later canonical negative constraint expose missing live section recovery.

Reviewed F-068 through F-072 and every terminal FABLE repair line: controlled tokens and rich records improve exactness, but action derivation, transition authority, state composition, secure restore, Discovery/cache interaction, and live section realization remain incomplete.
